ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS
September 202 6
DOB ISSUES MONTHLY ENFORCEMENT BULLETIN
Report Highlights DOB Enforcement Outcomes from September 2026
to Deter Bad Actors and Keep New Yorkers Safe
New York, NY – The New York City Department of Buildings released its enforcement
bulletin for September 2026, which provides highlights of the agency’s actions to
sanction and deter bad actors in the construction industry through the enforcement of
safety laws and codes of conduct. Today’s bulletin includes summaries of DOB-
imposed disciplinary actions, including penalties, license suspensions, and revocations.
The actions below represent a portion of DOB’s overall work to enforce the City’s
building codes and safety laws, in addition to the thousands of inspections conducted
and violations issued by the agency each month for illegal building and construction
conditions.
DOB completed several major enforcement actions in September, including:
 8 violations and $95,000 in penalties imposed for failure to safeguard
construction sites at 8 locations.
 6 violations and $243,750 in penalties, including daily penalties, imposed for
illegal alterations at 1 location.
 3 violations and $11,000 in penalties issued for illegal transient use, including
daily penalties at 1 location.
 1 padlock closure order issued for violating a stipulation agreement to cease
illegal storage at one location.
Below are individual enforcement highlights for September 2026:
Construction and Design Professionals
 DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) issued an Order of the Commissioner
demanding the Professional Engineer Allen Shinfeld produce special inspection
records for ten jobs that Mr. Shinfeld took responsibility for and signed-off on.
After SET interviewed Mr. Shinfeld regarding the documents produced, SET
found major code non-compliances, including knowingly or negligently making
false statements to the Department; taking responsibility for but failing to perform
or negligently performing special inspections; and failing to maintain and make
available for the Commissioner’s review the required records of special
inspections for a period of six years. Based on the non-compliances, SET filed a

petition at OATH seeking to permanently revoke all filing privileges. Before trial,
Mr. Shinfeld signed a Stipulation of Settlement and agreed to permanently
surrender all filing privileges.
 SET audited seven professionally certified applications submitted by Registered
Architect Brian Ill and found major code non-compliances, including filing
Alteration Type 2 applications despite proposing changes in use, egress, and/or
occupancy, which require Alteration Type 1 applications for a new or amended
Certificate of Occupancy; failing to provide two means of egress as required;
proposing plans that do not show enclosure of the interior exit stairway leading
directly to the exit discharge or the public hallway; proposing plans that indicate
insufficient primary entrance door maneuvering clearance; and various other
violations of code and rules, including the Zoning Resolution, Building Code, and
Administrative Code. Based on the audits, SET offered a voluntary surrender of
Professional Certification and Directive 14 privileges, which Ill agreed to.
 The Master Rigger license for George Cole was revoked by Order of the
Commissioner following a trial at OATH. Mr. Cole was found to have failed to
maintain required workers compensation insurance, failed to pay seven former
employees wages they were owed, forged and filed false certificates of insurance
with the Department and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, and
failed to collect, account for and pay over federal payroll taxes. Separately, Mr.
Cole was criminally convicted for this misconduct.
Bronx
 $80,000 in penalties imposed on Prakash 3250 LLC for violations recorded at
3250 Perry Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for illegal conversions after
finding the two units in the cellar converted to six dwelling units through the
addition of four Single Room Occupancies (SROs). Inspectors also issued
violations for lack of firestopping in the additional units and around vertical gas
risers between floors.
Brooklyn
 $25,000 in penalties imposed on Jun’s Construction Inc. for violations recorded
at 23 Ocean Parkway. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
after a 4’ x 8’ section of wood parapet fell to grade, and inspectors determined
that the panels of the sidewalk shed were shifting and/or defective.
 $12,500 in penalties imposed on Sunshine Constr USA Inc. for violations recorded
at 2745 Atlantic Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for inadequate public
protection after observing the 14-story pipe scaffolding on the site missing debris
netting and guardrails, and for failure to safeguard after observing Styrofoam
debris from the site scattered onto adjacent property.

 $10,000 in penalties imposed on MB Constrct/DSGN Sues LLC for violations
recorded at 141 North Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard a new building site after observing inadequate guardrails and lack of
fall protection while 6 workers were engaged in masonry work at the roof level,
and for toe boards missing from guardrail system.
 A closure order was rescinded for 354, 370, 372, 376 & 388 Ruby Street, a group
of vacant residential lots under a 2024 closure order for illegal use of contractor’s
yards and commercial vehicle storage in an R4 residence district. The property
owner and the multiple commercial tenants removed all the contractor’s
equipment, dumpsters and oil tanker trucks, and recission of the closure order
was executed once all violating conditions were addressed. Corrected conditions
pictured below.
Manhattan
 $20,000 in penalties sustained on West 125th Street Equities for violations
recorded at 353 West 125th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for an
outdoor advertising company that is prohibited in a C404 zoning district, and for
the outdoor advertising company’s failure to obtain an OA registration number
while engaging in the outdoor advertising business. Violating sign pictured below.

 $11,250 in penalties imposed on Baja 137 LLC for violations recorded at 137
West 19th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for illegal conversion after
finding multiple Class A units converted to short-term rentals on the building’s 5th
floor. DOB inspectors also issued violations for lack of required means of egress
on every floor, lack of automatic sprinklers and lack of automatic fire alarm
system as are required for transient use dwellings.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Alba Services for violations recorded at 262 5th
Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard the public during
crane operations after observing a tower crane operator lowering a 30-foot steel
beam without a sufficient flag person assigned to direct pedestrian traffic.
Queens
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on JLS Group Construction LLC for violations
recorded at 42-76 Hunter Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard after observing a mobile scissor lift that was unrestrained at a leading
edge on the 7th floor, endangering workers and the public.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on INC B36 Services for violations recorded at
131-20 40th Road. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard the
job site after plywood fell onto the street while the job site was closed, and
inspectors observed that the roof parapet on sidewalk shed was damaged and
inadequate netting on the scaffold.
 A closure order was executed at 78-05 149th Avenue, a vacant lot in an R4
district, after the owner failed to remove unregistered and unlicensed vehicles as
required under a stipulation agreement. Violating conditions pictured below.

 Illegal use was discontinued at 47-11 90th Street after commercial vehicle storage
and dead storage of motor vehicles were removed from a vacant lot in an R6B
residence district. Corrected conditions pictured below.

 A closure order was rescinded at 112-05 159th Street, property under a 2022
closure order for use of a contractor’s yard, commercial vehicle storage and junk
salvage storage in an R3A residence district. The property owner removed
multiple tenant businesses conducting industrial activity and addressed the
violating conditions. Corrected conditions pictured below.
 Illegal use of junk salvage storage was discontinued at 64-46 Alderton Street,
located in an R3-1 residence district. Following direct outreach, the owner agreed
to stop operating the recycling can business at the location. Corrected conditions
pictured below.
